name: mumbai-rent-vo-1
text: Twenty-six hundred square feet. South Mumbai. Rent... about thirteen hundred rupees a month. [short pause] Not a typo. Bloomberg found this family in twenty twelve, on Nepean Sea Road... where market rent was over one lakh rupees. How? In nineteen forty-seven, Bombay's rent law froze rents at nineteen-forty levels. Wartime prices... locked in for generations. Increases are capped at about four percent a year... on those tiny bases. One study found controlled rent can be one-thousandth of market rent. So landlords earn almost nothing... and repairs stop. Mumbai has about fourteen thousand old cessed buildings. [short pause] But here's the twist. The tenant holds the value. When a developer rebuilt that building... the family got about fourteen crore rupees to leave. Cheapest rent in India... or the most valuable lease? [pause] Twenty-six hundred square feet...
